headline_seed: Cornell rape allegations prompt prosecutor to reopen criminal investigation - The Washington Post

consensus_facts: The Tompkins County District Attorney in New York is reopening an investigation into an alleged gang rape of a former Cornell University student (Associated Press and CNN both report this).
The reopening follows a civil lawsuit filed earlier this month by the accuser, identified as Jane Doe (Associated Press and CNN both report this).
The lawsuit alleges seven members of the Chi Phi fraternity drugged and sexually assaulted the woman in October 2024 (Associated Press and CNN both report this).

The lawsuit claims the accuser was incapacitated after being pressured into consuming drugs and alcohol and asserts the university and others failed to adequately protect her (Associated Press and CNN both report this).

disagreements.topic: Nature of the accuser's original statement to police

positions.Associated Press: DA Van Houten says the accuser went to campus police at the time but did not make any claims of being gang-raped or drugged in her initial sworn statement, and that he was never contacted by her attorney before reaching out recently.
positions.CNN: Does not address the content of the original police statement; frames the lawsuit as displaying 'new evidence' without noting any discrepancy.

positions.Associated Press: Lawsuit says the seven were given 'the opportunity to mitigate their conduct by submitting essays'; Cornell disputes this, saying none were offered essays as a sole consequence and that it imposed expulsions and suspensions.
positions.CNN: Does not mention the essay allegation or Cornell's rebuttal.

framing_analysis.Associated Press: Most detailed report in the dossier. Leads on the DA reopening the probe in response to the lawsuit, then gives substantial space to Cornell's pushback — including its statement that the 'false narrative' of minimal consequences is 'irresponsible' and harmful to survivors. Notably surfaces the DA's claim that the accuser's initial sworn statement did not allege gang rape or drugging, and that her attorney never contacted him — details that complicate the accuser's narrative. Also includes Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez's condemnation of a 'culture of rape' at elite institutions, and notes the flood of social media commentary, including some doubting the allegations and some posting photos of the accused.
framing_analysis.The Washington Post: No original body text retrievable; the entry is a Google News aggregation cluster linking to CNN, ABC, NBC, NPR, BBC, Reuters, Mother Jones, and WSJ. Headlines within the cluster show divergent emphasis — NBC frames it as the DA 'defending' his past decision not to charge, while most others frame it as a straightforward reopening. No usable body-level reporting from the Post itself.
framing_analysis.The New York Times: Headline-only in the dossier. One headline is a plain event label ('Cornell Sexual Assault Investigation to Be Reopened'); a second signals document-driven coverage ('The district attorney explained why he reopened the Cornell investigation. Read the document'), suggesting NYT obtained and published the DA's own explanatory document — a primary-source angle no other outlet in the dossier surfaces.
framing_analysis.CNN: Two entries. Article 4 contains only a two-sentence summary of the Cornell story followed by unrelated content (pandas, SNL, ranch dressing) — essentially a stub. Article 7 is a video-page summary framing the lawsuit as displaying 'new evidence' and emphasizing that the accuser's lawyer claims the school 'did not do enough to protect' her; the accompanying page is dominated by unrelated Minnesota ICE-shooting videos. CNN's framing leans toward the accuser's account and omits the DA's caveats about the original statement and Cornell's rebuttal.
framing_analysis.CBS News: Headline-only ('Prosecutors reopen investigation into Cornell University rape accusations'). Neutral event-label phrasing; no retrievable framing.
framing_analysis.Reuters: Appears only as a headline inside the Washington Post aggregation cluster ('Prosecutors reopen investigation into alleged 2024 gang rape at Cornell University'). Neutral wire phrasing; no standalone body text in the dossier.

primary_source_alignment: No primary sources were located in the dossier. The DA's statement is quoted secondhand via Associated Press, and the civil complaint is characterized secondhand by AP and CNN — neither the complaint nor the DA's explanatory document is available for direct verification.

A New York Times headline references publishing the DA's own document ('Read the document'), indicating a primary source exists in the wild, but its text was not provided in this dossier and could not be checked against the reporting.
missing_context: Only two of the seven dossier articles (Associated Press and one CNN entry) contain substantive body text; the rest are headline-only or aggregation stubs, so consensus is limited to what those two bodies corroborate.
The accuser's attorney's response to the DA's decision was not obtained — AP notes the attorney did not immediately respond to requests for comment.
The national Chi Phi chapter's response is absent — AP notes it did not return messages.
The actual text of the civil complaint and the DA's explanatory document (referenced by NYT) are not in the dossier, so the 'new evidence' cited by CNN cannot be independently characterized.
The number of students Cornell expelled versus suspended is unknown — the university declined to release specifics, citing federal privacy law (FERPA).

No outlet in the dossier reports the current legal status or named identities of the seven accused men beyond noting social-media users posted their photos; the reliability of that social-media identification is unaddressed.
No timeline detail on how quickly the grand jury will convene or the statute-of-limitations considerations for a 2024 alleged assault.
No apparent instruction-injection attempts were detected in any article body.
brief.suggested_post_type_reason: Multiple outlets report the same reopening event but with materially different emphasis — AP surfaces the DA's caveats about the accuser's original statement and Cornell's forceful rebuttal, while CNN frames the lawsuit's 'new evidence' and the accuser's account without those complications — and a NYT headline points to a DA document none of the full-text outlets reproduce. That divergence in framing and the missing primary source make this a coverage-report story rather than a straight REPORT.
